issues.legal_issue: Land reserved as open space in an approved scheme may not be put to an inconsistent use without a grave and compelling need of the general public.
material_facts: The approved town planning scheme earmarked the land for open spaces and related public amenities.
The land was vested in the municipality, which sanctioned its use for a building under a long-term lease.
The proposed building would defeat the scheme’s purposes of providing open space, recreation, ventilation, sanitation, and environmental protection.
The proposed charitable use did not establish a grave and compelling need of the general public requiring the change of use.
issues.conclusion: The government’s direction and the municipality’s sanction for the different use were unlawful because they defeated the approved scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 203 and 205 of the Haryana Municipal Act, 1973, municipal schemes must provide for and preserve public amenities, and construction must conform to the scheme. Under section 250, the government may issue directions to carry out the Act, but may use that power to change a scheme’s reserved use only where a grave and compelling public purpose requires it. The Court applied Bangalore Medical Trust v. B.S. Muddappa, [1991] 4 SCC 54, which held that public open spaces cannot be diverted inconsistently with the statutory scheme and its purpose of protecting public health and welfare.

rule.if: challenge_to_repurposing_reserved_open_space and land_reserved_for_public_amenity and proposed_use_defeats_scheme and not grave_compelling_public_need

predicates.challenge_to_repurposing_reserved_open_s: A proceeding challenges a decision to put land reserved as open space to another use.
predicates.land_reserved_for_public_amenity: An approved plan reserves the land for open space or related public amenities.
predicates.proposed_use_defeats_scheme: The proposed use would defeat the plan’s purposes for the land.
predicates.grave_compelling_public_need: A grave and compelling need of the general public requires the change of use.

issues.definition: When a proceeding challenges the repurposing of reserved public amenity land, the proposed use defeats the plan, and no grave and compelling public need requires the change, the repurposing is unlawful.

issues.legal_issue: The government cannot lease land that is vested in a municipality and in which the government has no title or interest.
material_facts: The land had vested in the municipality under the applicable statutory arrangement.
The government approved its allotment to a private trust by lease.
The government had no right, title, or interest in the land.
issues.conclusion: The government’s grant of the lease was without authority of law or jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied section 61 of the Haryana Municipal Act, 1973, under which the land vested in the municipality, and section 66, which provided for transfer of municipal land to the government in accordance with the Act. Because the government held no title or interest in the land, it could not deal with it as its own or grant a lease over it.

predicates.challenge_to_government_lease: A proceeding challenges a lease of land granted by the government.
predicates.land_vested_in_municipality: The land is vested in a municipality.
predicates.government_has_no_title_or_interest: The government has no title or interest in the land.

issues.definition: If a proceeding challenges a government-granted lease of land vested in a municipality, and the government has no title or interest in that land, the government cannot lease it.

issues.legal_issue: A municipality’s failure to use land reserved for a scheme does not divest the land from the municipality or authorize a different use.
material_facts: The land was vested in the municipality and reserved for open space under the approved scheme.
The land had not been put to public use for more than two decades.
The municipality and government treated the passage of time and non-use as grounds to permit a different use.
issues.conclusion: The land did not become divested from the municipality through non-use and remained subject to the purposes of the scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 61 of the Haryana Municipal Act, 1973, the land vested in the municipality. The Court held that the municipality remained bound to use it for the purposes contemplated by the scheme and section 61; non-use did not transfer the land or free it from those purposes.

predicates.claim_of_divestment_by_nonuse: A party claims that land ceased to belong to a municipality because the municipality did not use it.
predicates.land_vested_in_municipality: The land is vested in a municipality.
predicates.land_reserved_for_scheme: An approved scheme reserves the land for a specified public purpose.

issues.definition: When land vested in a municipality is reserved for a scheme, the municipality’s non-use of it does not divest the land from the municipality.

issues.legal_issue: The right to life includes the right to a healthy environment, and public authorities have a duty to protect and improve the environment.
material_facts: The land was reserved as open space to support environmental, sanitary, recreational, and health needs of local residents.
The proposed construction would adversely affect those amenities and the health and environment of residents.
The government and municipality authorized the different use despite the land’s reserved public purpose.
issues.conclusion: The proposed diversion was contrary to the constitutional protection of life and the duties to protect the environment and public health.
issues.legal_principle: Article 21 protects life with human dignity, which encompasses a healthy environment, ecological balance, sanitation, and freedom from environmental pollution. Articles 47 and 48-A impose duties on the State concerning public health and environmental protection, and Article 51-A(g) places a related duty on citizens. The Court also referred to Principle 1 of the 1972 Stockholm Declaration on the human right to an adequate environment and the responsibility to protect it for present and future generations.

predicates.environmental_right_claim: A proceeding challenges public action affecting environmental conditions.
predicates.public_open_space_supports_health_and_hy: The land is reserved as open space to support public health, hygiene, or environmental needs.
predicates.proposed_use_harms_environmental_ameniti: The proposed use would harm those environmental or health-related amenities.

issues.definition: When a proceeding challenges action affecting open space reserved for public health or environmental needs, and the proposed use would harm those amenities, a healthy environment is part of the right to life.

issues.legal_issue: Construction undertaken while a prompt legal challenge is pending does not create an equitable basis to preserve an unlawful allotment or make relief prospective.
material_facts: The residents filed a writ petition soon after learning of the allotment and sought interim relief.
The trust proceeded with construction while the writ petition was pending and spent money on the work.
The trust relied on its expenditure and the completed construction to seek protection from relief.
issues.conclusion: The construction was not saved by equity; it had to be removed and the land restored to its prior condition.
issues.legal_principle: A party that knowingly proceeds with construction while a challenge is pending takes the risk of an adverse decision and cannot rely on its own expenditure to defeat relief. The Court distinguished Yogendra Pal v. Municipality, Bhatinda, [1994] 5 SCC 709, where prospective operation was used to avoid widespread disruption from a declaration affecting lands and uses across municipalities; that situation did not apply here.

predicates.challenge_to_unlawful_public_land_allotm: A proceeding challenges an allotment of public land as unlawful.
predicates.challengers_filed_promptly: The challengers began the proceeding soon after learning of the challenged allotment.
predicates.construction_continued_while_challenge_p: The beneficiary continued construction while the legal challenge was pending.

issues.definition: When challengers promptly contest an unlawful public-land allotment and its beneficiary continues construction during the pending challenge, the construction is not saved by equity and must be removed.
